reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
In a game, Mysong and Naoki are making problems. They each have four cards like these.

[1] [2] [3] [4]

The winner of the game is the person who can make the problem with the largest answer.

Mysong placed the cards like this.

[Image: Mysong's card placement]

Naoki placed the cards like this.

[Image: Naoki's card placement]

Write numbers in the squares below to show how you would place the cards to beat both Mysong and Naoki.

[Image: Blank addition grid]

descriptors: One of the following: 42+31; 41+32; 31+42; or 32+41
Combinations of the numbers 1, 2, 3 and 4. Every number is used only once.
Combinations of the numbers 1, 2, 3 and 4. One or more numbers are used more than once.
Combinations containing one or more numbers other than 1, 2, 3 and 4
Other incorrect

reference_items.figure_description:
Four square cards are shown in a row labeled with the digits 1, 2, 3, and 4.
Below are two vertical addition problems:
Under the heading "Mysong placed the cards like this.", two rows of two square cards form a vertical addition problem: top row has cards [4] and [3]; bottom row has cards [2] and [1], with a plus sign '+' to the left of the bottom row and a horizontal addition line underneath.
Under the heading "Naoki placed the cards like this.", two rows of two square cards form a vertical addition problem: top row has cards [3] and [1]; bottom row has cards [2] and [4], with a plus sign '+' to the left of the bottom row and a horizontal addition line underneath.
At the bottom of the item is an empty addition grid consisting of four blank squares arranged in two rows of two, with a plus sign '+' to the left of the bottom row and a horizontal addition line underneath.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

descriptors: Mysong. 64 and 55 are shown (or 9, which is the difference between 64 and 55) with a correct verbal explanation.

Mysong. 64 and 55 are shown (or 43 − 31 > 24 − 21) without any further explanation.

Mysong. The response gives no verbal or numeric explanation.
Other responses containing Mysong. For example, “because Mysong had the largest answer.”
Neither Mysong nor Naoki win.
Naoki. There may or may not be an explanation.
Other incorrect, including “both won.”

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Geometry Tiles
Instruction:

For this item, you have been given a piece of cardboard with 6 tiles like the ones shown below. Take the piece of cardboard, and punch out the 6 tiles.

If you do not have the piece of cardboard, raise your hand.

4 Triangle Tiles
[Image: Four triangle tiles]

2 Trapezoid Tiles
[Image: Two trapezoid tiles]

These tiles can be used to make new figures. One problem has been done for you

USE: 3 Triangle Tiles
MAKE: A trapezoid
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.
[Image: Example showing a trapezoid drawn on the grid]

Now try these problems.

A.

USE: 1 Triangle Tile and
1 Trapezoid Tile
MAKE: A 4-sided figure
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.

[Image: Triangular grid]

descriptors:
Correct 4-sided figure turned in any position
[Image: A parallelogram composed of one trapezoid tile and one triangle tile]
Makes a larger triangle
Makes a 4-sided figure, but not using the specified tiles, e.g., a larger parallelogram.
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)
Blank

reference_items.figure_description:
The stem includes four diagrams:
1. '4 Triangle Tiles': Four identical equilateral triangles of unit side length, arranged in a row pointing alternately up, down, up, and down.
2. '2 Trapezoid Tiles': Two identical isosceles trapezoids each composed of three equilateral triangle units (bottom base 2 units, top base 1 unit, legs 1 unit for the first one; and inverted with top base 2 units, bottom base 1 unit for the second one).
3. Worked example grid: An isometric grid forming a parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides of 3 units each and slanted sides of 2 units each, divided by dashed lines into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangles. In the top-right portion, a trapezoid made of 3 triangle units (top side 1 unit, bottom side 2 units, slanted sides 1 unit) is outlined in bold solid lines.
4. Part A response grid: An identical empty parallelogram-shaped isometric grid with top and bottom edges of 3 units, slanted sides of 2 units, divided into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangle units by dashed lines.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
For this item, you have been given a cardboard ruler. If you do not have the cardboard ruler raise your hand. Use the map below and your ruler to answer this set of questions.

Marytown is a new town. The people of Marytown are planning their new town. They decided to put the town hall halfway between the lake and the forest, as shown on the map below. They made their measurements from the X's.

Marytown

[Image: Map of Marytown]

Add a park, a library, and a school to the map of Marytown using the following information.

C. The school should be halfway between the park and the library. On the map, mark with an X where you would put the school and write school below the X.

descriptors: School equidistant from park and library, X to X, measures to differ no more than 4mm
School is not equidistant (+/- 2 mm) from park and library
Other incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)
Blank

reference_items.scoring_notes: Note: Park, library, and school need not to be in a straight line.
reference_items.figure_description:
A map of Marytown enclosed in an irregular rectangular border.
Near the top right inside the border, text states: "Scale: 1 cm represents 100 meters".
In the upper-left quadrant is a forest represented by a cluster of pine trees, with an "X" mark below it labeled "Forest".
Near the center of the map is an "X" mark labeled "Town Hall" below it.
In the lower-right quadrant is an outlined body of water with wavy horizontal lines inside, with an "X" mark directly above it labeled "Lake".
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
